title: JSFL: setFrameProperty/frame.tweenEasing 'ease' property unhandled — tween easing cannot be set via script
description:
In packages/authoring-ui/src/jsfl/runtime.ts, the setFrameProperty handler at line 940 handles: tweenType, label/labelName, labelType, actionScript/script, soundName, soundSync, soundEffect. It does NOT handle the 'ease' property.

Flash 8 JSFL supports timeline.setFrameProperty('ease', -100) to set the tween ease value (-100..100) on a motion or shape tween keyframe. The JsflFrame interface (line 175) also has no 'tweenEasing' property getter/setter, so frame.tweenEasing reads as undefined.

This means:
1. Any automation script that calls setFrameProperty('ease', n) silently fails (no warning, no-op).
2. frame.tweenEasing is always undefined regardless of actual tween ease.

Impact: scripts that configure easing on motion tweens (e.g. auto-generated tweens with custom ease) will produce wrong output — the compiled SWF will use linear easing instead of the authored value.

Fix:
1. In setFrameProperty, add a case for property === 'ease': parse value as a number clamped to -100..100, find the keyframe, and call mutateTimeline to update frame.motionEase.
2. Add a 'tweenEasing' getter/setter to JsflFrame interface and makeFrameProxy that reads/writes the governing keyframe's motionEase field.

Reference: Frame.motionEase (number, -100..100) is the JSFL 'ease' property name per Flash 8 documentation.
